title: HTTP/3 WebSocket Protocol Error Close Verification
verification_method: Focused HTTP/3 loopback test, RFC 9220 parser regression tests, SpecTrace JSON validation, generated coverage triage, and diff hygiene.
scope: This verification covers an accepted websocket Extended CONNECT tunnel whose application handler opts into protocol-error close mapping, receives a malformed unmasked client frame, writes an unmasked 1002 close frame, completes the writable side of the stream, and observes the parser failure.
preconditions: The WebSocket frame parser remains trace-owned by `VER-QUIC-RFC9220-0002`.
The WebSocket handler dispatch boundary remains trace-owned by `VER-QUIC-RFC9220-0003`.
The accepted tunnel application-close boundary remains trace-owned by `VER-QUIC-RFC9220-0006`.
expected_result: The focused loopback and parser tests pass, the new RFC 9220 protocol-error close requirement is trace-clean, SpecTrace validation accepts the artifacts, and diff hygiene is clean.
status_summary: The HTTP/3 server handler path now has locally verified opt-in protocol-error close behavior on accepted RFC 9220 tunnels. Evidence class is local same-process loopback over the repository QUIC transport; it is not external peer interoperability, published ProtocolLab evidence, or isolated-host proof.
